Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the NexGen Auto Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NexGen Auto's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Elena Vasquez, CFO; Marcus Lee, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Sofia Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:  
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Reflecting on Q3, we are proud of the significant strides NexGen Auto has made across all facets of our business. We have achieved remarkable progress in scaling vehicle deliveries to record levels with enhanced efficiency, expanding our charging infrastructure for superior utilization, strengthening our order backlog amid robust reservation momentum, optimizing raw material costs through resilient sourcing, delivering outsized revenue growth with margin expansion, advancing EV range and powertrain innovations, and executing on key operational milestones that solidify our market leadership. The market reception to our CyberHaul pickup has been overwhelmingly positive, with the associated fleet and consumer adoption far exceeding our initial estimates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our financial performance in greater detail.

Elena Vasquez:  
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. Let's start with the headline number: total revenue for the third quarter reached $28.4 billion, representing a robust 52% year-over-year growth from $18.7 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of accelerating revenue growth, outpacing the broader automotive industry's 8-10% global growth rate and surpassing even the strongest peers in automotive revenue expansion. 

Breaking this down by segment highlights our diversified revenue streams as a key differentiator in the EV landscape. Automotive segment revenue, our core engine, came in at $24.2 billion, up 61% year-over-year, driven by record vehicle deliveries of 512,000 units—a 58% increase from 324,000 units last year. Average selling price held steady at $46,500 per vehicle, reflecting a healthy mix of our high-margin premium models like the NexGen Model X all-electric SUV and the CyberHaul pickup, which ramped to 45,000 units delivered, capturing 12% U.S. market share in the heavy-duty EV truck segment ahead of competitors like Ford's F-150 Lightning and Rivian's R1T. 

We also recognized $1.8 billion in regulatory credit sales, up 25% year-over-year, benefiting from ZEV mandates in California, Europe, and emerging credits under the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act. This non-dilutive, high-margin revenue stream, at 95% gross margins, positions us favorably as peers like GM and Stellantis ramp their own credit generation. Energy generation and storage revenue hit $2.1 billion, surging 112% year-over-year, fueled by deployments of our next-gen Megapack 3.0 systems with 450 kWh per unit using LFP chemistry for superior cycle life. We shipped 18 GWh of storage capacity, including a landmark 5 GWh utility-scale project in Texas with ERCOT, and partnerships with solar developers scaled for grid stabilization amid rising renewables penetration.

Services and other revenue rounded out at $1.3 billion, up 35% year-over-year, from Supercharger network expansion to 65,000 stalls globally—up 40%—Full Self-Driving software subscriptions now at a 28% attach rate on new vehicles, and our over-the-air upgrade ecosystem generating $450 million in recurring, high-margin SaaS-like revenue. 

On a regional basis, North America contributed 58% of total revenue at $16.5 billion, up 67% year-over-year, propelled by IRA incentives averaging $7,500 per vehicle and our Fremont Gigafactory hitting 1 million annual run-rate capacity with gigacasting for Model Y. Europe was 22% at $6.2 billion, up 42% year-over-year, despite softening demand from subsidy phase-outs in Germany; our Berlin Gigafactory offset this with localized 2170-to-4680 cell transitions, boosting margins by 3 points. China grew to 15% at $4.3 billion, an explosive 89% year-over-year increase, where our Shanghai plant outproduced BYD's Blade battery volumes in the premium segment, aided by our dual-motor AWD tech commanding a 15% price premium over local rivals like NIO and XPeng. APAC ex-China and other regions made up the balance, with early traction in Australia's right-hand-drive CyberHaul.

Gross margins expanded to 21.4% overall, up 420 basis points year-over-year, with automotive at 19.8%—ahead of peers at 18.5% and legacy OEMs like Ford's 10-12% EV margins. This was underpinned by cost-down initiatives: a 25% reduction in battery costs via in-house 4680 cell production at 95% yield, vertical integration of structural packs, and a 40% drop in silicon carbide inverter expenses through our Texas supply chain reshoring. For Q2 context on margin trends, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 14.8%, up 320 basis points sequentially from Q1 and 410 basis points year-over-year, our highest since volume production launch, driven by fixed cost leverage from ramping over 85,000 vehicles at Gigafactory Nevada at 75% of 120 GWh capacity, improving product mix with higher-margin SUVs at 42% of volume, raw material deflation shaving 2% off COGS, and vertical integration insourcing 60% of battery pack assembly. North America margins stood at 17.1%, Europe at 12.2% amid tariffs, and we guide for further 100-150 basis point expansion in Q3 toward 15.8-16.3%, on track for 20%+ by 2026 via battery roadmaps to under $60 per kWh and software leverage.

Strategically, this revenue acceleration reflects our 'Scale or Fail' playbook. We've de-risked supply chains with $5 billion in U.S. cathode and separator localization, mitigating Red Sea disruptions. New product ramps like the $25,000 entry-level Model 2 for H1 2025 will drive volume-led growth targeting 2.5 million annual deliveries by 2026. Year-to-date, 9-month total revenue stands at $78.9 billion, up 49% year-over-year, positioning us for $115-120 billion full-year guidance, outperforming consensus by 15%. Our financial position remains strong, with $12.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We anticipate $30-32 billion for the upcoming quarter.

Next, we'll hear from Marcus Lee regarding the latest developments in our manufacturing operations.

Marcus Lee:  
Thank you, Elena. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at optimal levels to meet the surging demand for our vehicles. We've successfully implemented advanced automation technologies, resulting in increased production output and reduced cycle times. Gigafactory Nevada hit 1.2 GWh quarterly output, a 40% year-over-year increase, thanks to AI-optimized cell-to-pack assembly lines reducing scrap rates to under 0.8% and boosting throughput by 25%. We've produced over 5 million kWh of our NexCell 4680-style cylindrical cells cumulatively, with energy density surpassing 280 Wh/kg. This vertical integration slashed battery costs to $68 per kWh at the pack level, directly fueling margin expansion.

Following me, Dr. Sofia Chen will provide an update on our technological innovations.

Dr. Sofia Chen:  
Thank you, Marcus. Our R&D team is relentlessly pursuing breakthroughs in battery technology, autonomous driving systems, and vehicle connectivity. We've made outsized progress in electric vehicle range improvements and efficiency gains, where range anxiety remains a top barrier for 62% of buyers per recent studies. Our flagship platform has seen a compounded 22% range improvement over 18 months, outpacing the industry's 14%. The 2025 model-year Bolt achieves 412 miles EPA-estimated range, up from 340 miles, via a 15% denser 102 kWh NMC 9.0 pack with silicon-doped anodes. Fleet-wide energy consumption dropped to 198 Wh/mi, 16% better year-over-year and 28% above U.S. DOE averages, boosting gross margins by reducing battery material costs 11%.

These gains come from battery innovation with 65% transition to tabless 4680 cells for 96% usable capacity and 98% cold-weather retention; 800V SiC inverters at 94% efficiency improving regen by 22%; OTA updates optimizing torque vectoring for 8 Wh/mi urban savings; and aerodynamics with 0.198 Cd via gigacast modules lightening curb weight by 187 lbs. Regionally, this drove 35% U.S. sales surge, outselling competitors in Europe under WLTP, and narrowing gaps in China. We're allocating $1.1 billion capex for solid-state prototypes targeting 650-mile range by 2027, with RangePlus subscriptions projecting $250 million ARR. We unveiled the NexGen Autonomy Stack 3.0, achieving 99.7% disengagement-free miles on 12 million validation fleet miles, on track for unsupervised FSD beta in Q1 2025 unlocking billions in software revenue.

After me, Raj Patel will offer insights into our supply chain strategies.

Raj Patel:  
Thank you, Sofia. We have established a resilient and diversified supply chain network to mitigate risks and ensure the seamless flow of materials. Our proactive approach has enabled us to navigate global challenges effectively, with raw material costs per vehicle declining 14.2% year-over-year to $18,200 BOM average, battery cells at $92 per kWh. Lithium prices corrected 78% to $14,500 per ton, but we've reduced single-supplier dependency to under 15%, with 55% lithium from Australian offtakes at $18-22k/ton floors through 2027.

Regionally, 45% North American sourcing leverages IRA Section 45X for 70% cathode localization dropping cell costs 12%; 35% APAC with 200 GWh fixed at $75/kWh and 60% shift to low-cobalt LFP; 20% Europe/emerging with Umicore precursors. Initiatives include 65% LFP transition saving $1,200 per pack, Texas recycling recovering 95% metals at 40% below virgin costs, 70% hedging for 2025-2026 exposure, aluminum down 11%, and DLE pilots for 50% lower lithium costs. Copper headwinds added $150 per vehicle, but $2.5 billion capex for U.S. cathodes counters tariffs. We forecast 3-5% inflation in 2025 versus consensus 8%.

Next, Lisa Wong will share updates on our sales performance and market expansion initiatives.

Lisa Wong:  
Thank you, Raj. Our sales team has achieved remarkable success in expanding our market reach and driving revenue growth. We are seeing strong demand across regions, with total Q3 vehicle deliveries of 512,000 units globally, up 58% year-over-year from 324,000 and 12% sequentially, exceeding guidance. For context, in aligned Q3 metrics, we delivered 52,347 vehicles in premium segments, with Apex SUV at 28,456 units (54%, up 35% YoY), Pickup at 15,239 (29%, up 52%), and Sedan at 8,652 (17%). North America dominated at 67% or 34,912 units up 32% YoY via IRA and partnerships; Europe 20% or 10,567 up 22%; APAC 13% or 6,868 up 18%.

Order backlog stood at $28.4 billion or 285,000 vehicles at $99,500 ASP, up 12% sequentially and 22% year-over-year, with Model Y/compact SUVs at 62%, trucks at 25% up 35%, premiums at 13%. Net reservations hit 620,000, up 9% QoQ and 42% YoY, with 72% conversion. North America 68% up 16%, Europe 18% up 5%, China 12% up 28%. Inventory at 18-45 days best-in-class sustains demand.

Our EvoCharge network deployed 4,200 new stalls in Q3 to 28,500 total at 3,200 sites, up 32% YoY, with $285 million capex net $240 million post-IRA credits, on track for 18,000 YTD. Utilization reached 48% network-wide, up from 39% YoY and crushing industry 28-32%, with peaks at 72%. SuperEvo V3+ at 55%, regional NA 52%, Europe 44%, APAC 41%. Revenue $162 million up 55% YoY, ARPU $1,820, subscriptions $42 million at 68% margins. V4 rollout at 500 kW, AI scheduling, 75% renewables. Q4 guides 5,500 stalls at 55% utilization.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. To withdraw, star then two.

Analyst 1:  
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Can you elaborate on the order backlog trends and how reservation conversions are holding up amid higher interest rates?

Jordan Hale:  
Great question. Our global order backlog ended Q3 at $28.4 billion, about 285,000 vehicles at $99,500 ASP, up 12% sequentially from $25.3 billion and 22% year-over-year, even adjusting for FX. Model Y SUVs drove 62% at $17.6 billion up 18%, trucks 25% at $7.1 billion up 35% on 68% reservation conversions from 120,000 since launch, premiums 13%. Reservations at 620,000 net, up 9% QoQ and 42% YoY, 72% overall conversion with trucks at 78% via trade-ins. NA up 16% on IRA, Europe 5% on Berlin ramp shortening waits to 45 days at 71% conversion, China 28% on rebates. We've baked 75% conversions into FY guidance of 1.9-2.1 million deliveries, resilient despite rates via zero-interest pilots and 45-day turns.

Analyst 2:  
Thanks. On gross margins, what drove the expansion and how sustainable into next year?

Elena Vasquez:  
Margins hit 21.4% overall, automotive 19.8%, up 420 bps YoY from fixed cost leverage on 85,000+ production, Nevada at 75% capacity with CATL cells under $75/kWh, mix shift to 42% SUVs, raw deflation on lithium to $12k/ton, 60% insourced packs at 96.5% yield, warranty to 1.8%. NA at 17.1%, Europe 12.2% on tariffs, China 9.5%. Roadmap to 20%+ by 2026 via $60/kWh packs, 80% NA/EU sourcing, autonomy subs at 85% margins, next-gen architecture cutting BOM 15%. Q4 up another 100-150 bps.

Analyst 3:  
For manufacturing, how are yields and capacity ramps progressing?

Marcus Lee:  
Yields at 95-96.5% on 4680 cells, Nevada 1.2 GWh quarterly up 40% YoY, 1.2 million run-rate with AI lines at <0.8% scrap, 25% throughput gain. Cumulative 5 million kWh over 280 Wh/kg, enabling $68/kWh packs. Capex funds 2.5 million capacity by 2027.

Analyst 4:  
CTO, on range and efficiency, what tech is enabling the gains and competitive positioning?

Dr. Sofia Chen:  
22% range uplift to 412 miles on Bolt via 102 kWh NMC packs, 198 Wh/mi fleet efficiency. 4680 tabless at 96% SOC, 800V SiC at 94%, OTA AI shaving 8 Wh/mi, 0.198 Cd. Ahead of Model Y at 378 miles, competitive with Lucid at lower price. Tailored for NA highways, EU WLTP, China NEDC. Solid-state for 650 miles by 2027.

Analyst 5:  
Supply chain officer, raw material volatility—how are you managing lithium and nickel?

Raj Patel:  
Costs down 14.2% YoY to $18,200 BOM, cells $92/kWh. Diversified: 55% AU lithium fixed to 2027, 45% NA IRA-localized, 35% APAC LFP. LFP shift saves $1,200/pack, recycling 95% recovery, 70% hedged, DLE pilots. Inflation 3-5% 2025.

Analyst 6:  
Sales, charging network utilization details and revenue impact?

Lisa Wong:  
48% utilization up from 39% YoY, peaks 72%, NA 52%, V3+ 55%. Added 4,200 stalls to 28,500, revenue $162M up 55%, 68% margins, EvoPass 28% uptake. Flywheel for 14% higher LTV, 22% delivery conversions. Q4 55% target.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 7:  
Overall performance highlights—how does Q3 stack against goals?

Jordan Hale:  
Record $28.4B revenue up 52%, deliveries 512k up 58% or 68.5k in premiums up 62%, margins 21.4-28.1%, EBITDA 16.3%, $312M OCF, $12.4B cash. Apex SUV 32%, TerraX 42% up 95%, NA 54% share to 4.2%, Europe 71% growth, China 110%. Nevada 40% output gain, Autonomy Stack 99.7% miles, Redwood deal, DOE loan. On track for 1M run-rate 2026.

Analyst 8:  
Forward guidance on deliveries and charging?

Elena Vasquez:  
Q4 deliveries 58-62k premiums scaling to 220k FY, full-year 1.9-2M. Charging 5,500 stalls Q4 to 55% utilization, capex $220-250M 2025 with partners. FY revenue $115-120B, margins 27-29%.

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering exceptional results and creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NexGen Auto Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
